\cvsection{Professional Summary}

Backend engineer writing production Go since 2020, with 6+ years in fintech. At AbanTether (crypto exchange, 1M+ users), built the real-time balance retrieval service in Go --- per-network goroutine worker pools, buffered channels for backpressure, context-based timeout handling --- and designed gRPC and Kafka-based asynchronous communication across the wallet backend. Currently designing card authorization and settlement systems at Mili Gold, a payments platform with 25M+ registered users.

\skillline{Languages}{Go, SQL}

\skillline{Go Concurrency}{Worker pools, buffered channels, context cancellation with select, goroutine leak debugging with -race, DB-level locking for shared state}
\skillline{Data}{PostgreSQL (query optimisation, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, composite indexing, row-level locking), Redis, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, DynamoDB, MySQL}
\skillline{Messaging}{Kafka --- exactly-once, idempotency, DLQ, circuit breaker; gRPC interservice communication; event-driven architecture}
\skillline{Security}{HMAC request signing (service-to-service)}
\skillline{Payments}{Card authorization flows, settlement, core banking integration, idempotency, reconciliation, multi-currency ledgers}
\skillline{Infrastructure}{Docker (production, self-managed deployments), Kubernetes (day-to-day on platform-managed clusters), AWS EC2, Linux}
\skillline{Architecture}{API design, domain-driven design, hexagonal architecture (ports and adapters), saga pattern, transactional outbox, SOLID}

\cvsection{Key Project}

\jobheader{Milli Card --- Real-Time Asset-Backed Payment Card}{Mili Gold}{2024 -- Present}
\jobsub{Card authorization infrastructure integrating with a national core banking network (Shetab) to power a Visa-equivalent debit card backed by gold assets}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Designed the waterfall debit logic behind each authorization: debit the gold balance at a locked conversion price first, then fall back to the user's linked bank account
  \item The conversion engine debits atomically using PostgreSQL row-level locking (\texttt{SELECT...FOR UPDATE}) inside a transaction --- concurrent authorizations on the same balance serialize at the database, preventing double-spends without application-level locking
  \item Held the 98\%+ authorization success rate required by the bank's SLA, serving 25M+ registered users with 5,000+ daily transactions at launch
  \item Integrated with the local core banking system for settlement, clearing, and dispute handling
\end{itemize}

\cvsection{Professional Experience}

\jobheader{Senior Backend Engineer}{Mili Gold}{Nov 2023 -- Present}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Owned system architecture and API design across the platform's core services: the Milli Card pipeline, the withdrawal settlement engine redesign, and the real-time leaderboard
  \item Redesigned the withdrawal settlement engine from 34 states down to 8, using Kafka exactly-once delivery with consumer-side idempotency keys in PostgreSQL --- this ended the daily blocked-transaction firefighting on a platform with 25M+ registered users
  \item Designed gRPC contracts for interservice communication between the notification and user-engagement modules, simplifying integration and balancing load between services
  \item Took a PostgreSQL query from 4 minutes to under 1 second with EXPLAIN ANALYZE, plan rewriting, and a composite index
  \item Built the leaderboard on Lua + Redis with atomic ranking, which removed the distributed lock contention the old design suffered from
  \item Built an LLM-based document processing feature end to end, from schema design to deployment; cut manual data entry by roughly 40\% working closely to Data Science team.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{4pt}
\jobheader{Backend Engineer}{AbanTether}{Feb 2022 -- Nov 2023}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Designed gRPC interservice contracts and Kafka-based asynchronous event pipelines with DLQ and circuit breaker for reliable cross-service and partner-facing communication
  \item Built the real-time balance retrieval service in Go (Gin, Sqlx): per-network goroutine worker pools across 8 blockchain networks, each independently tuned for that chain's RPC rate limits; held sub-10ms p99 under load for 1M+ users
  \item Built a two-stage concurrent pipeline for the Personal Wallet: buffered channels carried computed balances from RPC-fetch workers to DB-writer workers, with the buffer exerting natural backpressure when persistence slowed
  \item Diagnosed a goroutine leak caught by the \texttt{-race} detector in staging --- a sender blocked forever on an unbuffered error channel after the receiver exited on context cancellation; fixed by sizing the channel to the worker pool count
  \item Designed a hexagonal architecture for the Personal Wallet's Tron energy management --- domain logic decoupled from the Tron RPC/SDK adapter --- to automate daily energy delegation and allocation across wallets, eliminating manual 24/7 monitoring
  \item Built the Personal Wallet platform from scratch to replace paid third-party wallet services --- cut that monthly spend by roughly 90\%, and wallet fraud incidents dropped to zero after launch
  \item Modelled the multi-currency wallet schema: 400K+ wallets across 8 networks with consistency guarantees
\end{itemize}

\vspace{4pt}
\jobheader{Backend Engineer}{NuraFinTech (Remote)}{Mar 2020 -- Feb 2022}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Built the trade audit pipeline in Go: append-only, immutable records giving full traceability across trader operations
  \item Used the transactional outbox pattern in Go to get zero-loss guarantees across banking integrations without distributed transactions
  \item Built the trader-facing dashboard backend in Go for real-time trade data
\end{itemize}

\cvsection{Projects}

\jobheader{Relocation Jobs (kuchup.com)}{Solo backend/infra project}{2026}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Diagnosed and fixed a production board-load regression on a single-host PostgreSQL deployment: eliminated 678 uncached per-request round-trips, cutting board latency from $\sim$90s to $\sim$1.7s, then caught a follow-up Redis cache-check that had reintroduced network I/O into the same hot loop
  \item Built production monitoring for a memory-constrained EC2 host on Grafana Cloud Free + Alloy --- cardinality-filtered container metrics, synthetic health checks separate from on-box probes, and a runbook after a disk-full incident caused a host hang (Cloudflare 522, not an app error)
\end{itemize}

**Phase 1 — JD + ATS lens** for justDice, **Backend Developer – Golang (f/m/d)**, Hamburg (visa + relocation called out). Posted 3 Sep 2026. No tailored CV saved yet.

Your instinct is right on **company DNA**, wrong on **what the screen will hunt for**.

justDice and adjoe are the same Hamburg / rewarded-mobile family (justDice is applike group, Bertelsmann-backed; adjoe is rewarded ads at 770M users). Both want production **Go**, Hamburg relocation, and someone who ships. The JDs diverge after that:

| | **adjoe (Catalog)** | **justDice (this role)** |
|---|---|---|
| Seniority | Senior, 5y backend / 3y Go | Backend, **2–3y Go** |
| Core bet | Kafka / events, sub-second APIs, DynamoDB+MySQL at huge scale | **Go microservices on AWS + K8s + Elasticsearch** |
| Infra | Terraform is a plus | **Terraform + Terragrunt are proficiency** |
| Named AWS | Spot, implied | **ECS, DynamoDB, CloudWatch** |

The CV you pasted is the **adjoe** tailored file (`go-final` master, Hamburg line, DynamoDB/MySQL on the skills line, Relocation Jobs project, intern dropped). Keep it as a draft reference. Do **not** reuse it unchanged: Kafka-heavy bullets that won adjoe are weaker here; ECS / Elasticsearch / IaC are the new screen.

Scoring below is against **`go-final`**, not the adjoe PDF. DynamoDB is on the adjoe skills line and **not** in the master — I am not awarding it unless you confirm you actually used it.

---

### Company thesis

They run **mobile gaming loyalty**: users play, earn real rewards, justDice captures engagement. The hire is a Go backend who can **plan and keep a microservice estate** on AWS/K8s with Elasticsearch in the path — not a Kafka/adtech specialist and not a pure payments engineer. They say they move fast, want ownership from day one, and will still talk to you if the CV is imperfect. The ATS will not be that kind.

### JD must-haves (what the screen tokenizes)

1. **Golang** (2–3 years, microservices)
2. **AWS** — especially **ECS**, **DynamoDB**, **CloudWatch**
3. **Kubernetes**
4. **Elasticsearch**
5. **Terraform / Terragrunt**
6. **Microservices** + architecture / design patterns
7. **Relational + NoSQL**
8. **CI/CD / DevOps**, tests, performance/scalability

### Requirements × evidence (`go-final`)

| Requirement | Wt | Evidence in master / project | Verdict | Pts |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Production **Golang** 2–3y | 18 | Go since 2020; AbanTether worker pools / Gin / Sqlx; NuraFinTech Go | **strong** | 18 |
| **AWS ECS, DynamoDB, CloudWatch** | 16 | AWS **EC2**, Amazon **SQS + DLQ**; kuchup on EC2 + SQS. No ECS, no DynamoDB in master, no CloudWatch (Grafana instead) | **partial** | 5 |
| **Kubernetes** | 8 | Skills: “day-to-day on platform-managed clusters.” No owned-cluster story. kuchup project master: *do not invent Kubernetes* | **partial** | 3 |
| **Terraform, Terragrunt** | 8 | Nowhere in master or project masters | **gap** | 0 |
| Relational **and** NoSQL | 10 | PostgreSQL (EXPLAIN, `FOR UPDATE`); MongoDB staging cache; Redis; Elasticsearch listed | **strong** | 10 |
| **Microservices** architecture | 12 | gRPC contracts, Kafka async, hexagonal Personal Wallet, service ownership | **strong** | 12 |
| Architecture / **design patterns** | 8 | Hexagonal, saga, outbox, SOLID | **strong** | 8 |
| **CI/CD** and DevOps | 8 | GitHub Actions; AbanTether owned Docker/deploy; kuchup: GH Actions + EC2 deploy. Not IaC | **partial** | 5 |
| **Elasticsearch** | 6 | On the Data skills line only — no ES bullet | **partial** | 2 |
| Fluent **English** + ownership | 6 | C1; “owned system architecture”; two years e2e on Personal Wallet | **strong** | 6 |
| **Total** | **100** | | | **69 / 100** |

**Match: 69 / 100 — stretch.** The Go + microservices + scale story is real. The **decisive gaps** are the ones this JD names as proficiency: **Terraform/Terragrunt**, **ECS / DynamoDB / CloudWatch**, and **Elasticsearch as work, not a skill-line token**.

justDice’s “not a perfect CV” line helps a human. It does not help ATS.

### Implicit signals (not spelled out, still scored)

1. **Hamburg / visa / hybrid 3 days** — they will check location intent in the first seconds. Your adjoe header already says Hamburg; `go-final` still says generic “EU relocation.”
2. **Quality via tests** — unit + integration is in “what you will do.” Master barely shows testing; kuchup’s 90% coverage gate is fair project evidence, not employment.
3. **Ownership without waiting for tickets** — “impact from day one,” hackathons, challenge how they work. AbanTether e2e ownership and kuchup incident work map here; payments domain does not.

### First-interview bar (what TA/HM tick)

- [ ] Writes **Go microservices**, not “Go listed among languages”
- [ ] Has **run something on AWS** they can talk about (they will ask ECS; EC2/SQS is the honest substitute)
- [ ] Can discuss **K8s** at working-knowledge level without claiming cluster ownership
- [ ] Has **relational + document/KV** war stories (Postgres + Mongo/Redis is enough if Elasticsearch is not faked)
- [ ] Sounds like someone who **owns production** (deploy, incident, performance) — they have a case study after TA

### ATS verdict on **unchanged** `go-final`

**No.** Headline is Go/Kafka/distributed systems; body is **fintech payments**. Kafka, Shetab, Milli Card, and 12 AbanTether bullets will not hit **ECS, Elasticsearch, Terraform, Terragrunt**. Elasticsearch is a skill-line orphan. Location line does not say Hamburg.

The adjoe PDF is closer (Hamburg, trimmed AbanTether, kuchup project) but still Kafka-forward and still missing the justDice infra cluster.

### Mirror target

**Go microservices + production ownership on AWS-shaped infra** — AbanTether Personal Wallet (concurrency, backpressure, e2e Docker/deploy) as the mirror role; kuchup only as **evidence** for AWS EC2, SQS/DLQ, CI, performance, observability — not as a fake employer.

Do **not** lead with Milli Card / Shetab. Do **not** copy the adjoe Kafka/DynamoDB emphasis unless DynamoDB is real work you can defend.

**Confirm before phase 2:** Did you actually use **DynamoDB** (adjoe skills line) or **Elasticsearch** beyond listing them? If not, we keyword-bridge from Mongo/Postgres/Redis and leave Terraform as an interview gap.

Go ahead to the next phase, or what should I change?

**Phase 2 — Master pick + mirror candidate**

DynamoDB stays off this CV. Listing it to clear ATS and then calling it a sample project in a **case-study round** is how this process fails: justDice names DynamoDB as a core AWS skill, and they will probe it. We keep the **69 / 100** score from phase 1 (DynamoDB was never counted). Elasticsearch stays only as the existing `go-final` skills token — no fake ES bullet.

### Recommended master

**`go-final`** — same as phase 1, no score correction.

It is the Go archive: production Go since 2020, AbanTether concurrency/microservices, Mili Gold architecture. `java` / `fullstack` would bury the Golang must-have. Your adjoe PDF is a **skimmed, Hamburg-targeted cut** of this master, not a second master. We reuse its shape (Hamburg line, Projects, intern dropped) and change the keyword bet from Kafka/DynamoDB to **Go microservices + AWS-shaped production**.

### Mirror experience

**AbanTether — Backend Engineer (Feb 2022 – Nov 2023)**

That is the only role that looks like this JD: Go services, gRPC, worker pools, hexagonal ports/adapters, you owned Docker and deploys. Mili Gold is more recent and stronger on architecture/scale, but the story is **payments + Kafka + Java (MilliGallery)** — that is the adjoe-adjacent narrative, not justDice’s ECS/K8s/ES estate.

Reframe angle: you built and ran **Go microservices** with backpressure, timeouts, and e2e deploy ownership — the closest honest stand-in for “robust, scalable Go services on AWS,” without claiming ECS, Terraform, or DynamoDB.

### Project evidence

**`relocation-jobs` (kuchup.com)** — AWS **EC2**, Docker image split, **GitHub Actions** CI (90% coverage gate), Amazon **SQS + DLQ**, Grafana Cloud + Alloy (not CloudWatch), board latency **~90s → ~1.7s**. Explicitly **not Kubernetes**. Use as facts for 1 mirror bullet and/or a short Projects block. Not an employer.

MilliGallery project masters are Java/payments — drop for this Go role.

### Pull list (real evidence → justDice story)

1. AbanTether: Go balance-retrieval service, per-network goroutine pools, **sub-10ms p99**, 1M+ users  
2. AbanTether: two-stage pipeline, buffered channels, MongoDB staging + PostgreSQL source of truth  
3. AbanTether: **owned Docker / deploy / incidents** for two years  
4. AbanTether: hexagonal Personal Wallet (domain vs RPC adapter)  
5. kuchup: production performance + AWS EC2/SQS/CI/observability (project facts only)

### Skim-budget preview (`go-final` as-is)

| Block | Bullets now | Budget | Flag |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Mili Gold (most recent) | **9** | 5–7 (soft 8) | Over — Java MilliGallery + mentor are first cuts |
| AbanTether (mirror) | **12** | 5–7 including +1–2 new (soft 8) | Hard fail if shipped |
| NuraFinTech | 3 | 1–3 | OK, maybe 2 |
| Simurg intern | 1 | 0–2 | Drop (adjoe already did) |
| Key Project: Milli Card | 4 | keep short or cut | Weak for this JD (Shetab/gold card) |

Phase 3 will add **1–2** AbanTether bullets, then propose KEEP/DROP so AbanTether lands at ~7 and Mili Gold at ~6. Default recommendation: **accept the trim**.

### Gaps (interview only — not on the CV)

- **Terraform / Terragrunt** — no evidence; do not list  
- **ECS / CloudWatch / DynamoDB** — you have EC2, SQS, Grafana; DynamoDB is learning-only  
- **Elasticsearch as a system you ran** — skills line only  
- **Kubernetes** — platform-managed day-to-day; kuchup is Docker/EC2, not K8s  

If they ask AWS: EC2 + SQS + self-managed Docker, and kuchup ops. Do not open with DynamoDB.

### Sections to keep (from `go-final` + adjoe shape)

Keep: header (Hamburg + visa, as on the adjoe file), summary, Core Skills, Professional Experience, Writing, Education, Languages.  
**Drop intern.**  
**Add a short Projects block** (kuchup, 2 bullets) — already on the adjoe CV; it is the honest AWS/CI/performance surface this JD wants.  
**Key Project (Milli Card):** keep only if we cut it to 1–2 lines, or drop in phase 3 so page-1 skim is Go/AWS, not gold cards.

Go ahead to the next phase, or what should I change?
